76806.explanation: The first rite of Hajj is entering ihram - a pilgrim's sacred state - when crossing the outer boundaries of Mecca called Miqat.

76807.explanation:
Surah Nasr is one of the short surahs in the Quran that are knoen as Mufassalat. The surah praises Allah for leading numerous
people to Islam. This surah is also known as "The Victory" as in the victory of Islam as it refers to the conquest of Mecca where
Muslims beat the enemies of Islam.

76808.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76808.explanation:
The Jahiliyyah Arabs worshipped three main goddesses: al-Lat, al-Manat, and al-Uzzah. These goddesses were considered the
daughters of Allah.
However, as-sanat is not recognized as a goddess by the Jahiliyyah Arabs. Therefore, the correct answer is as-
sanat.

76809.explanation: A Muslim is only permitted to marry his late wife's sister.

76810.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76810.question_text: In the science of Hadith, the next Sahih on authenticity is
76810.explanation:
In the science of Hadith, the next Sahih on authenticity is Hasan.
Note that there are three primary ways to determine the authenticity(sihha) of a hadith: by attempting to determine whether
there are "other identical reports from other transmitters", determining the reliability of the transmitters of the report; and the
continuity of the chain of transmission of the hadith.

76811.explanation: (2:183) Believers! Fasting is enjoined upon you, as it was enjoined upon those before you, that you become God-fearing.

76812.explanation:

76813.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76813.explanation:
Imam an-Nasa'i, a noted collector of hadith (sayings and actions of Prophet Muhammad), spent most of his life in Khurasan. He
was born in Nasa, a city in Khurasan, and travelled extensively through the Islamic world to collect hadith. He eventually settled
in Khurasan, where he spent his remaining days.

76814.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76814.question_text: Permanent exemption from Ramadan fast may be occasioned by
76814.explanation:
Even though fasting in Ramadan is mandatory upon every functional and able Muslim, Allah Almighty has pardoned and excused
certain people from the act of fasting if they are unable to fast due to certain legitimate reasons. Individuals facing senility and old
age are essentially exempt from fasting. With old age comes weakness, terminal illnesses, loss of mental faculties and extreme
fragility, hence, it is believed that people in their old age are not required to fast at the cost of their health.

76815.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76815.question_text: The following Suwar begin with divine command to the Prophet except Surah
76815.explanation:
Suratu ad-Dua did not begin with divine commandment to the Prophet. Surah Ad-Duha was revealed to the Prophet(S.A.W.)bto
relieve him of these negative feelings and to give him hope, positivity and the assurance that Allah is with him no matter what.

76816.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76816.question_text: Which of the following is not a form of shirk according to the Qur'an?
76816.explanation:
Shirk in Islam refers to the sin of practicing idolatry or polytheism, i.e., the deification or worship of anyone or anything other
than the singular God, Allah. Therefore, Trinity and Polytheism are forms of shirk. Atheism, although not a form of shirk, is also
not in line with Islamic teachings. However, Monotheism, which is the belief in one God, is the fundamental belief in Islam and is
not a form of shirk.

76821.explanation: According to the Prophet, the greatest Jihad is to battle your own soul to fight the evil within yourself.

76827.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76827.explanation:
The Prophet, peace be upon him, was once asked by a man to give him advice. The Prophet told him, "La taghdab!" Which means,
"Don't be angry!" But the man didn't listen, and kept on repeating his request. The Prophet, peace be upon him, just kept on telling
him the same answer, "Don't be angry!

76828.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76828.question_text: The Surah which begins with four oaths is
76828.explanation:
The Surah which begins with four oaths is Surah at-Tin. The Surah starts with the oaths "By the fig and the olive, And [by] Mount
Sinai, And [by] this secure city [Makkah]". Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.

76829.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76829.question_text: The Prophet lost his wife Khadija in the year
76829.explanation:
Khadija died in 'Ramadan of the year 10 after the Prophethood', i.e., in November 619 CE. Muhammad later called this tenth year
the 'Year of Sorrow', as his uncle and protector Abu Talib also died at this time. Khadija is said to have been about 65 years old at
the time of her death.

76830.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76830.question_text: Who among the following played a major role in the transmission of Hadiths?
76830.explanation:
After the death of Muhammad, Aisha is regarded as the most reliable source in the teaching of the Hadith. Aisha's authentication
of Muhammad's ways of prayer and his recitation of the Qur'an allowed for the development of knowledge of his sunnah of
praying and reading verses of the Quran.

76831.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76831.question_text: The supererogatory prayer with a single rak'ah is Salatul
76831.explanation:
Witr (Arabic: j3) is an Islamic prayer (salat) that is performed at night after Isha (night-time prayer) or before fajr (dawn prayer).
It has just one rakah.

76832.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76832.question_text: A Juz' of the Qur'an is sub-divided into the following except
76832.explanation:
A Juz' of the Qur'an is not sub-divided into Manzil. A Juz' is one of the thirty parts of the Qur'an, each part is further divided into
two 'Hizb' making it a total of 60 Hizb. Each Hizb is then further divided into four quarters, making a total of 240 quarters in the
entire Qur'an. On the other hand, Manzil is a different system of dividing the Qur'an based on the places where the Prophet would
stop and take a rest during his recitation of the Qur'an.

76833.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76833.question_text: The reign of Caliph Uthman b. Affan is known for
76833.explanation: He centralized the administration of the Caliphate and established an official standard version of the Qur'an.

76834.explanation: Imam Bukhari died in 870 C.E. while Imam Muslim died in 875 C.E.

76835.explanation: Since Jummah is just two rakahs, the total will be 15 instead of 17.

76837.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76837.question_text: How many times does the word al-Qadr occur in Qur'an chapter 97?
76837.explanation: The word al-Qadr occurs three times in Qur'an chapter 97.

76838.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76838.question_text: Halimah, the wet nurse of Muhammad (S.A.W.) hailed from the Banu
76838.explanation:
Halimah al-Sa'diyah (Arabic: ull 4ql), was the foster-mother of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. Halimah and her husband
were from the tribe of Sa'd b. Bakr, a subdivision of Hawazin (a large North Arabian tribe or group of tribes).

76840.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76840.explanation:
The Tahajjud is a special night prayer which is recommended(but not compulsory) for all muslims. Known as the best among the
voluntary prayers, the Tahajjud is prayed after Isha (the obligatory nightly prayer) and before Fajr(the obligatory morning
prayer).

76849.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)

76849.explanation: Suratud-Duha(Q.93) has 11 verses in total. If the last verse is removed, the remaining verses are 10.

76850.explanation:
Suratul-Fatihah(Q.1:5) translates to 'You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help', which is an admonishment to Muslims
to worship none except Almighty Allah.

give thanks and praises to Allah

76851.explanation:
The Prophet Muhammad(S.A.W.) commanded knowledge upon all muslims(male and female), and urged them to seek knowlege as
far as they could reach, and also to seek knowledge at all times.

76852.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76852.question_text: To seek divine guidance, muslims are encouraged to perform Salat
76852.explanation:
Salat al-Istikhara, which translates to prayer of seeking counsel, is a prayer recited by muslims who are in need of guidance from
Almighty Allah when facing a decision in their life.

76853.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76853.question_text: Makkah is referred to in Qur'an chapter 95 verse 3 as the city of
76853.explanation:
Makkah is referred to in Qur'an chapter 95 verse 3 as the city of security. The verse says 'And [by] this secure city [Makkah],'
which implies that Makkah is a city of security.

76854.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76854.question_text: The capital of the ancient Ghana empire was
76854.explanation:
The capital of the ancient Ghana empire was Awkar. The Ghana Empire was located in what is now southeastern Mauritania,
western Mali, and eastern Senegal. Its capital city was Awkar.

76855.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76855.explanation:
In Islam, voluntary fasting is highly encouraged on Mondays and Thursdays, not Fridays or 'Id days. 'Id days are festive days in
Islam where fasting is actually prohibited. The day before Ramadan is also not specifically encouraged for fasting. Therefore, the
correct answer is 'Mondays'.

76856.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76856.question_text: The last verse of Suratut-Tin describes Allah as the
76856.explanation:
The last verse of Suratut-Tin (The Fig) in the Quran describes Allah as the 'Judge'. The verse is 'Is not Allah the most just of
judges?' (95:8). Therefore, the correct answer is 'Judge'.

76857.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76857.question_text: The first king of the Mali empire to accept Islam was
76857.explanation: Mansa Musa was the first king of the Mali empire to accept Islam.

76867.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76867.explanation:
Qada is not a voluntary but obligatory fast. It is a fast that is observed as a make up fast after Ramadan to compensate for any
missed fast or any shortcoming during Ramadan fast.

76871.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76871.question_text: 'Alam yajidka yatiman fa'awa(Q.93:6) refers to Muhammad (S.A.W.) as
76871.explanation:
'Alam yajidka yatiman fa'awa(Q.93:6) is a verse from the Quran which translates to 'Did He not find you an orphan and give [you]
refuge?' This verse refers to Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) as an orphan, which is the correct answer.

76875.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76875.question_text: The period between the advent of Islam in Arabia is referred to as Jahiliyyah because Arabia
76875.explanation:
Jāhiliyyah, in Islam, the period preceding the revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad. In Arabic the word means
"ignorance," or "barbarism," and indicates a negative Muslim evaluation of pre-Islamic life and culture in Arabia as compared to
the teachings and practices of Islam.

had no inspired Prophet and revelation
was surrounded by water in the West and South

76877.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76877.question_text: The SIXTH verse of al-Fatiha is a prayer for
76877.explanation:
The sixth verse of al-Fatiha is 'Guide us on the Straight Path'. This verse is a prayer for guidance, asking Allah to guide us on the
right path, the path of those who have received His grace. Therefore, the correct answer is 'Guidance'.

76878.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76878.question_text: Which of the following Suwar contains ELEVEN verses?
76878.explanation:
Suratul-ad-Duha contains 11 verses
This Surah, revealed in Makkah, is a message of hope and reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) during a period of
distress. It highlights Allah's care and support for His Messenger, urging him to be patient and reminding him of the blessings that
Allah has bestowed upon him.

76879.explanation:

76881.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76881.question_text: A memorizer of the Qur'an is known as
76881.explanation:
Hafiz is an Arabic word used to identify the one who entirely memorizes and recites the Qur'an, the holy book of Muslims, which
is over 600 pages with more than 6,000 verses. The word hafiz is also used for those who memorize the sayings of Prophet
Muhammad in certain numbers, but these are rare.

76883.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76883.question_text: Thre prostration performed while reading the Qur'an is Sujud
76883.explanation:
The prostration of recitation(sujud tilawa) is a prostration(sujud) which occurs during the ritual Tilawa of Quran in Salah or
outside it.

76884.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76884.question_text: The first revelation is contained in Suratul
76884.explanation:
The first revelation of the Qur'an, which was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) by Angel Jibril (Gabriel), is contained in
Suratul 'Alaq. The first five verses of this Surah were the first verses of the Qur'an to be revealed.

76885.subject: Islamic Religious Knowledge (IRK)
76885.question_text: A'ishah the daughter of Abu-Bakr was born in the year
76885.explanation:
A'ishah the daughter of Abu-Bakr was born in Mecca in 614 CE. She was the daughter of Abu Bakr and Umm Ruman, two of
Muhammad's most trusted companions.
